name: Fixed platform topsides and substructures
applications: shallow and medium water fixed platforms
principle: Fixed offshore platforms combine a substructure (welded steel jacket, or concrete gravity-base structure) founded on or pinned to the seabed with a topsides deck carrying drilling, production and power. Jackets are launched or lifted in place and piled through legs; topsides are built as integrated or modularised decks and set by float-over or lift. Design is governed by ISO 19902 (steel) and structural reliability against extreme wave, wind and fatigue loads; weight control and deck elevation against air gap are the persistent constraints.

process_steps.name: Jacket fabricated and launched or transported to site
Jacket levelled and pinned with foundation piles
Topsides integrated or modularised, set by lift or float-over

limitations: installation weather windows and vessel availability dominate the offshore schedule
decommissioning obligations are engineered in from the start on many regimes
advantages: proven over decades; steel jackets span almost all practical fixed-platform water depths
modular topsides reduce offshore hook-up and commissioning
